## So what is the composable unit?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- Turn the question around. A `Distributions.jl` distribution is
  already an interface the whole of Julia understands, so write the
  epidemiology as distributions and the probabilistic programming
  language becomes optional rather than load bearing
- `CensoredDistributions.jl` does not depend on Turing. Nothing in the
  source mentions it. A Turing model can still use the distributions,
  and nobody has to install Turing to get them
- A composed delay comes back as
  `IntervalCensored{Truncated{PrimaryCensored{Convolved{...}}}}` and
  every generic function you already use still works on it

::: {.callout-note}
The language was always meant to be backend agnostic. This is what
taking that seriously looks like.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Where this is going**

- `CensoredDistributions.jl` and `ConvolvedDistributions.jl` are
  registered and cover censoring and sums of delays. Neither requires
  the other to work
- `ComposedDistributions.jl` for a natural history written as chains,
  branches and outcomes. It fails all six autodiff configurations on
  `main` today
